description: The Federal Reserve Payments Study is an ongoing effort by the Federal Reserve to estimate aggregate trends in noncash payments in the United States, giving policymakers, the industry and the public a periodic benchmark of developments in the U.S. payments system. The latest release, of July 2026, gives national payment volumes and top-line data for calendar years 2015 to 2024 and trends in the number and value of noncash payments from 2000 to 2024 by instrument, including credit cards (general purpose and private label) and prepaid debit cards (including electronic benefits transfer). Estimates come from the Depository and Financial Institutions Payments Survey and the Networks, Processors, and Issuers Payments Surveys; markers show survey years and lines between them are interpolations. Figures and data are free on the Federal Reserve site, and as U.S. Government works they are in the public domain. Caveats: estimates are national aggregates, some years are interpolated, and the pages read do not give file formats. For simulation it provides the national mix and volume of payment instruments, used to size disruption impacts on card and other payment networks. Related catalogue records include the BIS CPMI Red Book statistics and Fedwire statistics.
